title: Threat Brief: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP: CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619 (Updated November 19)
summary: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are Critical vulnerabilities in PHP, a scripting language used globally for web servers and CMS systems.
body_markdown:
## Executive Summary


Unit 42 is aware of two critical vulnerabilities in PHP: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, referred to as PHP2Shell. Both are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities rated as 9.2 (CVSS 4.0). We encourage reviewing the[PHP Group’s security advisory and patching guidance](https://www.php.net/index.php) .


PHP is widely used across web servers and content management systems globally. We recommend assessing your exposure to these vulnerabilities and patching immediately.


Palo Alto Networks has evaluated our product portfolio regarding this issue. Refer to our


[security advisory](https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618) for the most up to date details.


- [CVE-2026-109618](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-109618) involves a remote code execution vulnerability where handling out-of-memory errors via longjmp()


leaves request memory uninitialized due to improper control flow management, allowing attackers to reliably achieve RCE using out-of-memory (OOM) triggers.
- [CVE-2026-109619](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-109619) describes a remote code execution vulnerability where longjmp()


fatal error handling leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. These regions can later be read or branched on during subsequent requests, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary code.


At the time of publication, Palo Alto Networks[Cortex Xpanse](https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/p/XPANSE) has identified the presence of over 22.6 million exposed instances potentially vulnerable to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 based on our telemetry.


#### Update October 29, 2026


As disclosed in our[security advisory](https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618) , the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities are being actively exploited against PAN-OS management interfaces that are exposed to the internet.[Dream Research](https://dreamgroup.com/blog/chained-php2shell-exploit-roots-25-servers) has reported a campaign in which attackers chained PHP2Shell with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation vulnerability to gain root access. Unit 42 has independently verified the same attacker’s tooling and confirmed the reported results.


By default the management interface is not exposed to the internet per[security best practices](https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/best-practices/10-1/administrative-access-best-practices/administrative-access-best-practices/deploy-administrative-access-best-practices) ; customers should immediately remove public internet access to management interfaces if it is enabled. Customers should also restrict management access to trusted internal IP addresses, and apply available PAN-OS fixes addressing PHP2Shell. Customers who have applied the available patches are not affected. These fixes interrupt the observed exploit chain. Our security advisory provides affected versions, patch availability and mitigation requirements. The Workarounds and Mitigations section of our[security advisory](https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618) also provides details of how Advanced Threat Prevention signatures provide coverage against this vulnerability.


Only a small fraction of a percent (approximately .02%) of our global installed base has internet-facing management interfaces configured and were impacted. Each of these customers has been individually contacted by our teams. We will continue to investigate and provide any necessary updates as they become available.


Palo Alto Networks customers receive protections from and mitigations for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 in the following ways:


- [Advanced WildFire](https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/wildfire)
- [Cortex XDR](https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/p/XDR) and[XSIAM](https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/p/XSIAM)
- [Cortex Cloud](https://cortex-docs.paloaltonetworks.com/cortex-cloud-docs) and[Prisma Cloud](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/prisma/cloud)
- [Cortex Xpanse](https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/p/XPANSE)
- [Advanced Threat Prevention Plus with Frontier Virtual Patching](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/network-security/harnessing-ai-for-prevention-introducing-frontier-virtual-patching/)
- [Next-Generation Firewall](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/network-security/next-generation-firewall) with[Advanced Threat Prevention](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/network-security/advanced-threat-prevention)
- [Device Security](https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/iot/getting-started/iot-security-solution)
- [Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense](https://www.paloaltonetworks.ca/unit42/prepare-for-emerging-risks/continuous-frontier-ai-defense)


Palo Alto Networks also recommends assessing your exposure to these vulnerabilities and patching immediately.


Organizations can access tailored adversary intelligence, direct analyst consultations, and specialized exposure tracking through[Unit 42 Threat Intel Services](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/unit42/threat-intelligence) and our[Deep and Dark Web Service](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/resources/datasheets/unit-42-deep-and-dark-web-service) .


The[Unit 42 Incident Response team](https://start.paloaltonetworks.com/contact-unit42.html) can also be engaged to help with a compromise or to provide a proactive assessment to lower your risk.


**Vulnerabilities Discussed**[CVE-2026-109618](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tag/CVE-2026-109618/) ,[CVE-2026-109619](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tag/CVE-2026-109619/) , **[PHP2Shell](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tag/PHP2Shell)**

### Advanced WildFire


The[Advanced WildFire](https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/wildfire) machine-learning models and analysis techniques have been reviewed and updated in light of indicators associated with chained PHP and kernel vulnerabilities.


### Cortex XDR and XSIAM


[Cortex XDR](https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/p/XDR) and[XSIAM](https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/p/XSIAM) are designed to help protect against post-exploitation activities using the multi-layer protection approach. provide multilayered protection against post-exploitation activities. Cortex XDR also provides visibility into installed software across endpoints and servers, including on-premises and legacy environments, to help security teams identify systems running vulnerable PHP versions and prioritize remediation.


### Cortex Cloud and Prisma Cloud


[Cortex Cloud](https://cortex-docs.paloaltonetworks.com/cortex-cloud-posture-management/vunerability-management/vulnerability-management-in-cortex-cloud) and[Prisma Cloud](https://docs.prismacloud.io/) help identify vulnerable PHP versions across code, registry images and runtime instances. Cortex Cloud's Supply Chain Attacks Portal helps teams identify affected assets and take action to prevent vulnerable components from being reintroduced. Additionally, Cortex CLI integrates into CI/CD pipelines to scan images and enforce policies that block vulnerable images before they reach registries and runtime environments.


### Cortex Xpanse


[Cortex Xpanse](https://docs-cortex.paloaltonetworks.com/p/XPANSE) can identify exposed devices on the public internet and escalate these findings to defenders. Customers can enable alerting on this risk by ensuring that the PHP Attack Surface Rule is enabled. Identified findings can either be viewed in the Threat Response Center or in the incident view of Expander. These findings are also available for Cortex XSIAM customers who have purchased the ASM module.


### Next-Generation Firewall


[Next-Generation Firewall](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/network-security/next-generation-firewall) with the following security subscriptions can help block the attacks:


- [Advanced Threat Prevention Plus with Frontier Virtual Patching](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/blog/network-security/harnessing-ai-for-prevention-introducing-frontier-virtual-patching/) since 10:21 p.m. PT on October 20, 2026, via Threat ID[543004](https://threatvault.paloaltonetworks.com/?query=543004) .
- [Advanced Threat Prevention](https://www.paloaltonetworks.com/network-security/advanced-threat-prevention) with best practices since October 21, 2026 via the Threat Prevention signatures listed in full in our[security advisory](https://security.paloaltonetworks.com/CVE-2026-109618) .


### Device Security


[Device Security](https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/iot/getting-started/iot-security-solution) is designed to proactively protect the specialized device attack surface of operational environments, providing deep visibility into industrial protocols, actionable risk insights, and adaptive security enforcement across all OT and IoT assets.

##### October 25 Update


Unit 42 reported earlier that we had observed post-compromise activity that we initially thought was related to the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. What researchers saw was an attack against a European government agency executed in the context of a vulnerable PHP application. This led us to believe that it was exploitation of those vulnerabilities. We are unable to confirm that initial access is associated with the specific PHP2Shell CVEs. We have retracted our previous update from October 23.
